purpose: Authoritative-vendor industrial-edge and IoT delta. Adds EMQX Neuron, HiveMQ Edge, Cumulocity Platform and Cumulocity Edge at spec-verified only. All reuse existing protocol profiles; no sandbox or tenant credentials were used. Writes, management/control/provisioning/agent actions and broad cross-scope reads remain disabled.

systems.name: EMQX Neuron (formerly NeuronEX)
systems.evidenceNote: Current EMQX Neuron documentation identifies a plant-floor industrial edge gateway with 100+ southbound industrial protocols, MQTT/Sparkplug B, Kafka, HTTP and OPC UA northbound paths. Its REST API conforms to OpenAPI 3.1 and uses JWT authentication. RBAC provides a Viewer role corresponding to REST GET requests only, while device-control and OPC UA/MQTT paths can also carry writes. Manufacturing WFM therefore uses only Viewer GETs and approved read/subscribe data-plane paths behind the customer edge. No Neuron instance was authenticated or queried.

requiredPermissions: dedicated EMQX Neuron Viewer identity with authentication enabled and no use of the default administrator credential
REST GET operations only; no create, modify, delete, configuration or device-control requests
MQTT/Sparkplug subscribe-only topics over authenticated TLS and OPC UA Browse/Read/Subscribe only with authenticated encrypted sessions
Kafka consume-only access where used; no producer, rules, sink, plugin or management authority
dataAvailableOrExpected: device, node, group and tag metadata for connected PLCs, CNCs, robots, meters and other equipment
live and buffered industrial tag values with source/device context
normalized MQTT/Sparkplug streams and OPC UA hierarchy exposed from heterogeneous southbound protocols
approved data statistics, runtime health and alarm/status context through read-only APIs
processed or aggregated edge outputs where configured, marked separately from raw observations
automationOpportunities: reuse one edge abstraction across legacy PLC, CNC, robot and meter estates rather than building machine-specific cloud connectors
adjust labour demand and redeployment recommendations from actual machine and line state
correlate downtime, throughput and utility signals with labour cost and shift outcomes
accelerate site and work-centre mapping from device/group/tag hierarchy
use locally buffered telemetry for reconciliation after outages without treating replay as live state
savingsHypotheses: reduce bespoke machine connector engineering by consuming Neuron's normalized northbound data
reduce paid idle labour by matching staffing to actual machine availability
reduce overtime caused by late recovery visibility
reduce integration and support effort across mixed legacy protocols
reduce cloud exposure to low-level plant networks
dataGaps: worker, payroll, absence, roster and skills truth normally remains outside Neuron
tag naming, group hierarchy and semantic meaning are customer-specific
processed/aggregated values require provenance and cannot be assumed raw
offline MQTT cache can replay historical values after reconnect
southbound quality depends on each driver/device configuration
constraintsRisks: Neuron is plant-floor infrastructure and remains behind a customer/site edge boundary
Viewer exposes broad GET visibility, so customer-specific tag/resource allowlists are still required
authentication can be disabled by deployment configuration and must be verified enabled
default administrator credentials must never be used by WFM
MQTT, OPC UA and device-control surfaces are bidirectional-capable and require technical read-only enforcement
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse REST/OpenAPI, MQTT/Sparkplug, OPC UA and Kafka profiles for a thin Neuron adapter with version/capability discovery, Viewer-role verification, REST operation allowlists, topic/node filters, TLS/certificate validation, hierarchy fingerprints, source/ingestion timestamps, replay-age watermarks and raw-versus-derived provenance. Obtain an authorised lab or customer edge before promoting beyond spec verification.

systems.name: HiveMQ Edge
systems.evidenceNote: HiveMQ Edge documentation describes an industrial MQTT gateway with adapters including OPC UA, Modbus, S7, ADS/TwinCAT, EtherNet/IP, HTTP(S), file and BACnet, plus Unified Namespace topic hierarchies. Admin REST RBAC gives the user role read access to configuration and GET APIs while POST/PUT require higher privilege. Some protocol adapters are bidirectional, including MQTT-to-OPC-UA southbound writes. Manufacturing WFM therefore consumes only read-only REST metadata and approved MQTT subscriptions behind the customer edge. No HiveMQ Edge instance was authenticated or queried.

requiredPermissions: dedicated HiveMQ Edge read-only user role or equivalently constrained OIDC/LDAP-mapped role
REST GET operations only; no POST, PUT, adapter start/stop, mapping, policy or configuration changes
MQTT subscribe-only ACLs for approved namespace prefixes over authenticated TLS
no southbound MQTT-to-OT mappings, OPC UA writes, bridge changes or Data Hub policy mutation
dataAvailableOrExpected: MQTT telemetry normalized from OPC UA, Modbus, Siemens S7, ADS/TwinCAT, EtherNet/IP, HTTP, file, BACnet and other adapters
Unified Namespace topic hierarchy that can represent enterprise, site, area, line and asset context
source timestamps/status metadata where supplied by industrial adapters
approved read-only adapter, bridge and mapping metadata for implementation diagnostics
buffered messages after connectivity interruptions where the licensed capability is configured
automationOpportunities: use the customer's Unified Namespace to auto-suggest site, line and work-centre mappings
derive staffing and redeployment recommendations from normalized machine state without direct PLC access
correlate labour, throughput, downtime and energy across heterogeneous equipment
reuse existing MQTT topic governance for multi-site implementation
reconcile buffered data after outages while preventing stale replay from triggering live labour actions
savingsHypotheses: reduce bespoke device integration through one governed MQTT projection
reduce implementation mapping effort by reusing ISA-95-style namespace hierarchy
reduce paid idle and overtime by aligning labour to actual line state
reduce support effort through standardized MQTT observability
reduce direct cloud exposure to industrial protocols
dataGaps: workforce/payroll/skills/absence truth remains outside HiveMQ Edge
topic semantics and namespace quality depend on customer design
not every protocol adapter exposes identical timestamp or quality metadata
offline buffering is deployment/licence dependent
REST configuration visibility is not evidence that a telemetry topic is semantically trustworthy
constraintsRisks: HiveMQ Edge remains inside the site/plant security boundary
read-only REST role still sees broad configuration and requires customer-approved endpoint scope
MQTT bridge and protocol adapters can be bidirectional, so WFM must never rely on UI-level read-only behavior alone
OPC UA anonymous mode may exist southbound but production WFM does not accept anonymous OPC UA evidence
buffered/replayed MQTT data must retain source time and freshness
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse REST and MQTT profiles for a thin HiveMQ Edge adapter with RBAC verification, GET-only operation allowlists, topic ACL checks, namespace/ISA-95 mapping fingerprints, MQTT v3/v5 compatibility, source/ingestion timestamps, dedupe and replay-age controls. Keep southbound device/control and configuration surfaces disabled until separately authorised and evidenced.

systems.name: Cumulocity Platform
systems.evidenceNote: Cumulocity publishes OpenAPI-described REST APIs for inventory, measurements, events, alarms and related IoT resources, plus MQTT connectivity. Global and inventory roles can constrain ordinary API access, but current vendor documentation explicitly warns that Notifications 2.0 permissions can receive device data outside assigned inventory roles and that DataHub offloading does not incorporate base collection inventory-role access restrictions. Manufacturing WFM therefore uses only tenant/device-scoped REST reads and approved MQTT subscriptions; broad notification/DataHub read paths are separately disabled pending equivalent scoping evidence. No Cumulocity tenant was authenticated or queried.

requiredPermissions: tenant identity with READ-only inventory, measurement, event and alarm permissions limited by customer-approved inventory roles/device groups
MQTT subscribe/read-only device or tenant scope where required, with TLS and customer-approved authentication
no device operations, command/control, inventory mutation or administration
no Notifications 2.0 subscription or DataHub access unless a separately reviewed constrained projection proves equivalent tenant/device scope
dataAvailableOrExpected: managed objects/digital twins for devices, assets, groups and relationships
measurements and time-series sensor or production values
events and alarms with device/asset context
custom fragments and customer-specific device attributes
MQTT telemetry and connection metadata where enabled
automationOpportunities: map device groups and digital-twin relationships to sites, areas and work centres during implementation
adjust staffing/redeployment from measurements, alarms and production events
forecast downtime recovery and overtime risk from operational history
correlate energy/utility measurements with shift staffing and output
combine multi-site IoT evidence with labour and finance attribution without changing device control
savingsHypotheses: reduce device-by-device integration by reusing the customer's Cumulocity inventory and device model
reduce idle and overtime cost through earlier production-state visibility
reduce manual site/asset mapping through device-group hierarchy reuse
improve labour-to-output and labour-to-energy attribution
reduce custom reporting joins by normalizing IoT events into WFM objects
dataGaps: worker/payroll/absence/skills and authoritative roster data usually remain outside Cumulocity
custom fragments and device types are tenant-specific
legacy inventory-role searches may require following pagination even through empty intermediate pages
device telemetry quality and semantics depend on upstream integrations
Notifications 2.0 and DataHub security scope differs materially from ordinary inventory-role constrained APIs
constraintsRisks: Notifications 2.0 permissions can bypass assigned inventory-role device scope
DataHub offloading/query access can expose data irrespective of base collection inventory-role restrictions
MQTT/device APIs can support operations and control; WFM remains subscription/read-only
tenant, region and custom schema must be bound explicitly and never inferred across customers
rate limits, pagination and custom-fragment schema drift require resumable cursors and fingerprints
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse REST/OpenAPI and MQTT profiles for a thin Cumulocity adapter with tenant/region binding, inventory-role scope verification, device/group traversal, pagination checkpoints including statistics.next behavior, custom-fragment schema fingerprints, read-only MQTT topic mappings and operation allowlists. Keep Notifications 2.0 and DataHub disabled behind the cross-scope-read gate until an authorised tenant proves an equivalent constrained projection.

systems.name: Cumulocity Edge
systems.evidenceNote: Cumulocity Edge 2026 is the single-server on-site variant of the Cumulocity platform and can operate on local networks or in fully offline/air-gapped environments. Vendor documentation lists native REST and MQTT, local operational storage, streaming analytics and OPC UA. The same product also includes Edge Agent remote management, cloud data broker and device-management/control capabilities. Manufacturing WFM therefore treats Edge as a customer-edge data source and consumes only approved local REST/MQTT/OPC UA reads; operator, remote-management and device-control paths remain disabled. No Edge deployment was authenticated or queried.

requiredPermissions: local Edge tenant identity restricted to READ-only inventory, measurement, event and alarm resources for approved device/site scope
MQTT subscribe-only over authenticated TLS and OPC UA Browse/Read/Subscribe only with named authenticated encrypted sessions
no Edge Agent remote management, Kubernetes/operator administration, device operations, cloud data-broker writes or OPC UA/MQTT southbound control
no DataHub or other broad cross-scope read channel unless separately reviewed and constrained
dataAvailableOrExpected: local device/asset inventory and relationships
measurements, events, alarms and streaming-analytics outputs collected while cloud connectivity is unavailable
native MQTT telemetry and OPC UA-connected industrial data
local operational history for site resilience and reconciliation
approved Edge health/connectivity context for data-freshness decisions
automationOpportunities: keep local workforce intelligence supplied with production state during WAN/cloud outages
use a common Cumulocity canonical adapter for cloud and Edge while enforcing different network/security boundaries
adjust staffing/redeployment from low-latency local machine state
reconcile offline history after reconnect without treating backfill as current state
reduce data movement by consuming only WFM-relevant local projections
savingsHypotheses: reduce disruption and manual reconciliation during WAN outages
reduce cloud integration engineering by reusing the cloud/Edge API model
reduce latency in labour redeployment decisions from on-site telemetry
reduce unnecessary data transfer by normalizing locally
reduce bespoke OPC UA/MQTT integration where Edge already provides the abstraction
dataGaps: authoritative worker, payroll, absence, skills and roster data generally remains external
local device hierarchy/custom fragments remain customer-specific
offline history must carry source time, ingestion time and replay age
cloud/Edge release and optional feature availability can differ
single-server topology has different availability/scaling characteristics from cloud
constraintsRisks: Edge is customer-controlled on-site infrastructure and must never be scanned directly from the WFM cloud
remote management and cloud data broker can perform actions beyond WFM's data needs
OPC UA and MQTT are bidirectional-capable and require operation-level read enforcement
air-gapped deployments require customer-edge execution, local credential handling and deferred evidence upload
backfilled data after reconnect must never masquerade as live machine state
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the Cumulocity REST/OpenAPI and MQTT mapping logic plus OPC UA edge profile, but bind execution to the customer edge with local version/capability discovery, read-only operation allowlists, authenticated encrypted OPC UA, source/ingestion/replay metadata and offline checkpoints. Exclude Edge Agent/operator/remote-management/device-control paths and obtain an authorised Edge lab/site before promotion.
